text: I love how review geeks write their "pro" audiophile reviews for what is to me an entry/mid level Around-the-Ear Headphones. That being said I gave these headphones 5 stars as deservedly so. I'll tell you why in the 4 categories Amazon splits review stars into. I am not a tech geek or audiophile. I enjoy listening to music and watching movies on my laptop. If you want studio quality sound for studio work, buy studio headphones for $300+ more. Comfort: 5 stars Amazingly comfortable. The first day I had them I listened to music while I lifted weights in the morning. Had no problem with them being cumbersome or in the way at any point. I used them later on in the evening to watch a Dexter marathon on my laptop. I had them on for about 4 hours straight and the only thing I can say negative is that my ears started getting sweaty. But that might even be a good thing as this can refer to the seal of the ear pads being fully encapsulated. Not once did I feel uncomfortable. The adjustable neoprene-like band is a nice touch for heads of all sizes. I have a bigger head and a lot of headphones I try to use end up getting uncomfortable at the top. Not these. The around the ear design is flawless. Covered my ears completely and were very cushion comfortable. I LOVE the braided rope cord. It does not tangle and looks very sheik. Durability: 4.5 stars I can't imaging what it would take to break the frame of these headphones. They are made of a stretch nylon material that literally twists and shapes any way you pull it. Very cool. I haven't had these for very long so i don't know how the small parts will hold up. There are a couple of hinges that could fail down the line but that goes for most other headphones too. The aluminum type cover for the phone jack did come off the first day I had it as all that is keeping it on there is some cheap glue. Get a drop of super glue in there and that problem is solved. The stretch nylon is basically plastic so if you get them scratched, that cool see through smoke look is tarnished for good. Sound Quality: 5 stars Again, I am rating this based on the price point. And at $60, it is superb. I have listened to Bose Quiet Comforts and Beats Studio Pros and yes they were phenomenal but they were also $250-$300. More expensive. For how much more you would spend, I don't feel the sound is that much better for that much money. I didn't find anything funky with the lows or bass as some have said. I used it with my Macbook, iphone, ipod and Nintendo DS. The music quality is great but the movie sound quality is even better. It's like being in a small theater with surround sound. Every footstep, leaf crunch, and breath is picked up crystal clear and action scenes are much more lively. Again for the money, the sound is outstanding. Noise Cancelling: 4.5 stars Rated this high because they don't claim to be "Noise Cancelling" headphones. But with the phones on listening to music at a comfortable level...your friends will have to raise their voices to get your attention if you're not looking at them. In an airplane, it cancels out flight noise but you can still hear the "seat belt" tones while watching a movie. Though they are not "Noise Cancelling" phones, they do a great job of cutting out unwanted outside noise. Overall = 4.75 stars Very happy with the product. I asked an associate at Best Buy if anyone had returned these and she said no. They are one of very few items that do not have a return scan. That speaks volumes for the product and customer satisfaction. Definitely recommend these for anyone who wants to greatly enhance their mobile music and movie listening experience for very cheap.

text: I've waited for a couple of months to review these because I wanted to see how they lasted with more use. These were my first foray into completely wireless earbuds, and overall they were a great investment, and they are my go-to's every day for earbuds. First the pros: the battery life is exceptional. I have never had the battery run out on me, and I've worn them for several hours at a time with no dip in performance. I'll plug the case in to charge once a week or two weeks, just whenever I think about it, and it's always been enough to last until the next time I think about charging it. I haven't used the feature of charging my phone with the case, but it's nice to have the security that I could do so if need be. I did realize after a while that though the earbuds are magnetic, there's certain pins that have to line up in order for them to connect to the case and charge, and they don't always line up if they're just dropped into the slot. Usually I set the tips of the earbud into its slot and let the rest fall into place, then wait for the red light to come on to let me know it's connected. I haven't had this gap in connection lead to me having an uncharged earbud, but it did confuse me when I tried to play something from my phone and found the sound was still going to the earbud in the case. These are definitely hardy - a new issue I had to get used to is that, because these are not connected with a wire (obviously), I can't hang them around my neck when they're not in use, so if I stop in the middle of using them, they end up in my pockets. This eventually led to one of them getting thrown in the washer along with my shorts, and I didn't realize until the washer had halfway filled up with water that it was missing. I fished it out of the bottom of the machine and dried it, and it connected and worked. I set it in a cup of rice for about 12 hours just in case, but I don't think it really needed it. That was about two months ago, and I've never had a problem with that earbud from the incident. The range of the earbuds is actually in my experience a little more than the description says, but it mostly has to do with what obstructions may be in the way between the device and the buds. Sometimes I can go 100 feet with nothing in between and hear everything fine; sometimes I go 30 feet with two walls in between and it starts to break up. I've had one instance of it breaking up in one earbud and not the other, so that one side of the audio was 1 second behind the other side, and it was extremely disorienting. Just quirks of technology. The sound quality is good; I'm not necessarily an audiophile, but the sound from these buds are on par with, if not better, than all of my other past earbuds. If I have the earbud firmly pressed into my ear, it's pretty noise canceling - I can't hear someone behind me talking to me - but as I mention below, that placement is not comfortable for long periods of time. Cons: I was apprehensive about if they would fit in my ears, because I have slightly oddly shaped ears (not too big or small, just weirdly shaped), and I was sort of right. These will definitely stay in if I push the earpiece far enough into my ear for it to create a suction, but after 15-20 minutes that gets uncomfortable. If I put them in my ears normally, usually one side or another will start to get loose, so they aren't ideal for if I were doing something with a lot of continuous movement - say, a long run or rock climbing. I do wear these when I'm working out every time, and they work for me mostly, but that's mainly because I do primarily strength training that doesn't have a lot of high-speed or jostling movements, and where there's usually ample time for me to readjust a falling earbud. For just being stationary, especially for shorter periods of time, they're basically perfect. It's a very slight annoyance that when both sides are removed from the case, they automatically connect to your device, but when only one side is taken out you have to manually select it from the Bluetooth menu - but that's really just super minimal, it takes about two seconds to do it. A slight and specific idiosyncrasy: I use Spotify primarily for my music, and for some reason when these earbuds connect to my phone, Spotify identifies them as a car audio system and starts its "CarPlay" procedure, which is to auto-play whatever was being played before once the app opens. I don't mind this; it's one less thing I have to do; it's just kind of odd. Overall a great buy, and at a good price!

text: These are good headphones for the price. I have bought 3 pairs for friends and family. The original pair is still kicking after probably about 10 years! They are no Seinheisser for quality, but they are inexpensive and still are decent. One note about these headphones is that they only come with a headphone jack so that you can't plug them into the AV port. This will only allow you to listen to the TV on the headphones and will turn off the TV speakers. So this means that only the person with the headphones can hear. You will need to buy an additional cable to plug into the AV port ([[ASIN:B000I23TTE 2 x RCA Male, 1 x 3.5mm Stereo Female, Y-Cable 6-Inch]]) so that you can have the person with the headphones and a less hearing impaired person both watching TV at the same time. Keep in mind that these headphones are analog and if you go with the AV port, it has to be the AV port on the cable (or satellite) box because the new TV's are digital. It took me a while to figure this out! The headphone jack will work, but the AV cables won't. The box acts as a converter. This presents a problem if you have other devices (DVD or VCR) plugged directly into your TV, then the headphones won't work unless you plug them into that device. It can be a pain in the neck to switch them if you watch a lot of movies, but the digital headphones are a lot more expensive.

text: I hate writing reviews, but this item is worth it. Hopefully, my review will be useful. Buying this thing is a steal. It's actually the PX100 model, but named differently, less expensive and with a microphone. And don't worry about "iPhone" thing in the spec. It will work everywhere. Plugs are compatible (i.e. you will hear stereo, if plug it in a computer or other MP3 player). For those, who are not familiar with PX100 (original, not PX100-ii): It's not a typical crappy pair of headphones you can grab in a Target for $20-50. First of all, the sound is terrific for this price (I know what I am talking about, because I also own a pair of Sennheiser HD580). Of course, don't expect it to be as detailed as the sound in top Sennheiser models (HD595, HD580, HD600, HD650, HD800). But at least it's accurate. (Recently I've purchased a pair of Alessandro headphones for $100. In the audiophile community they are believed to be a very good tradeoff between the price and the quality. I tried them. The sound of piano was so wrong, that I decided to return them immediately.) The design is perfect. If you are buying headphones for traveling, it's far better than everything else out there. They are foldable and designed to be stored in a compact hard case (included). My only concern is reliability. Wires are so thin that you probably need to be accurate (although my previous PX100 broke only after 3 years of everyday use). But for less than $40, it's not a big issue. Overall it's undoubtedly a 5-star item. I will be very disappointed if Sennheiser decides to discontinue this model. Update: the foam has completely disintegrated => -3 stars

At first, it wasn't such a big deal, but it gotten worse and worse, and the headphones got less and less comfortable to wear as this process continued. I looked for replacement pads. There are cheap knock-offs on Amazon with reviews saying they don't isolate sound as well as the original, so that's a no-go, so I looked at the official store: Audio Technica sells replacement pads for a whooping 70GBP (about 87USD)! That's waaaaaaay too much. So, my verdict is: If you want really good headphones (and don't mind paying a ridiculous amount of money for replacement parts), buy these. But if you want something that will last *more* than two years, maybe these are not the best choice. Update (2017): The earpads are now starting to fall off the headphones, which makes things even worse. text: These are the best in-ear headphones I've ever owned. I've gone through Shures, Etymonics, Ultimate Ears, V-Moda and Zune in-ear headphones and the Klipsch, highly recommended by Amazon users, have been the best. I read all of the reviews before making my purchase decision and am glad I did. My four must-haves for in-ear headphones are: 1) Noise cancelling - block outside noise as well as contain the sound of whatever I'm listening to (hey, I have manners). I use earbuds for commutes on public transit and assholic cell phone use has sadly become a standard soundtrack in Toronto, which I find intolerable. Wearing these earbuds I could not hear babies crying, girlfriends chewing out their boyfriends, people eating obnoxiously noisy food or sirens passing by. I would not wear these outdoors for running because the noise cancelling is just too good - I reserve them for indoor workouts on a stationary treadmill. I have even used them on flights as earplugs only - they really do muffle the sound by at least 10-20db. These fit snugly and I have worn them for 10+ hours a day sometimes without any soreness or discomfort like you'd sometimes experience with other brands. 2) Excellent sound quality - I hear things using these that I don't otherwise hear listening to the same songs on a stereo. Try listening to Elliott Smith's "Pictures Of You", Telefon Tel Aviv's "Stay Away From Being Maybe", Beck's "Mixed Bizness" or Lady Gaga's "Bad Romance" on Klipsch vs. stereo and you'll see what I mean. When properly inserted, I only have to turn the volume to the 1/3 mark. 3) Solid cord construction - these fare pretty well even though I've been tossing them into the bottom of my book bag for a month now, and there is a 2 year warranty, which I think is excellent value. The cords on my V-Modas and Ultimate Ears both shredded in no time and exposed the wire inside, and had to either be replaced (UEs - twice) or thrown out. I'm not concerned with not getting my money's worth here - if these last 2 years I will be very impressed! And if they don't, well...I have a warranty. 4) Volume/remote control - the controls are outstanding and each function works on my iPhone 3GS, iPod Classic and iPod Shuffle (3rd gen. - yes, I have a lot of electronics). On the iPhone I'm able to quickly toggle between music enjoyment and phone calls. Sometimes when I'm at home I take calls on my iPhone and can do things like lie in bed chatting for an hour handsfree and also look things up online, instead of greasing up the side of my iPhone with the oils on my face or accidentally hanging up on the person. The microphone is great and you don't have to hold it up to your mouth for it to work - no one has complained about the volume of my voice. On the iPod & Shuffle, I'm able to adjust the volume, start/stop, skip and fast forward songs (this last feature on Shuffle only). The only reason I conceded to buying the new Shuffle (which I use for workouts) in the first place was because I owned these earbuds and knew I could control playlists and songs via the cord (otherwise you can't use it with anything but the earbuds it comes with, and as we all know, Apple earbuds ARE HORRIFYINGLY BAD AND SHOULD CEASE BEING PRODUCED - sorry, got angry there). I can fast forward or rewind songs, skip tracks, hear voiceovers and toggle through my various playlists with the controls. The cord length is also just right and there is no tangling or fiddling required. I'm glad I read the reviews thoroughly before buying these - for this reason I knew to try inserting the earpieces at 180 degrees for an optimal fit. Had I only tried the standard fitting I would surely have been disappointed by the sound isolation and quality. Seriously - try this first before dismissing these as ill-fitting. I bought these for $120CDN at Apple Store (Amazon.com does not ship to Canada). Money is no object to me where good headphones are concerned, but for this price I was really startled to receive such a high quality product!

text: June 1st 2022 update. The battery has gotten pretty bad. I keep losing one or the other ear bud. I even lost the case. That is not the fault of these earbuds of course. As i kept misplacing one of the pieces, or even just choosing to use 1 ear bud, i slowly starting to notice the earbuds becoming desynced. Not that they are unusable. There has always been a bit of a resync moment but it seens to be more frequent and at the same tine the battery seems to deplete quicker. I think this could be a sync issue since i have used the earbuds individually but either way it is a issue The battery to each ear bud has gotten to half or a quarter as long full charge. Overall i guess i would pass but also at $20 I'm not at all upset and feel i got my money worth for aboit a ueaf of use and going (til replaced) I bought these AND THEN read the reviews after they shipped already. Hardly any of the criticism and low rates i read were accurate to my experience so far after little over a week of daily use. This is my first ever pair of "air pod" like earphones. They do get uncomfortable sometimes, actually pretty often at first, maybe I've gotten more use to it. Just rotating it around in my ear until it was comfortable works. I've worn them through a full sleep, full shifts at work, but not running yet but i feel like they wouldn't fall out easily. The case doesn't feel cheap per se but it doesn't feel quality, it is fairly small and if it wasnt $20 i would be very scared of losing it or breaking it, and the case battery isn't great but at least the earphones themselves have a good battery life. My final issue is every once in a while (its happened about 3 times in the week) the audio cuts for a fraction of a second and i am not sure if it is the earphones or my phone getting a notification or something, it doesn't bother me but i'm sure it would bother some people. Actually 1 more criticism, they aren't very loud but they block out outside noise well enough that its not a major issue but when i first turned them on i didn't realise my ohone was at full volume, i thought it was like 30% or maybe 50%, it was 90%. I was sorely disappointed but for $20 i can still call it a great purchase. The battery life and sound quality are good. They fit very snug in my ears. You can actually have 1 on at a time while the other is off. I read people giving 1 star because only 1 earbud worked and that you had to use a Philip's app to use them instead of Bluetooth, what? No app needed, both ears work, just turn them on 1 at a time and they sync perfectly. When i first started using these and watching videos on my phone the latency was weirdly not bad, lips and audio were so close in sync i was kind of shocked, its not consistently that great though (Bluetooth headphones in general). I can walk to the other side of our small house without losing connectivity. I've had other devices not reach as far. Overall they work great, biggest issue is they get uncomfortable, i won't stop using them, i won't be seeking replacements while i have these, i would recommend them as long as they are under $50, Update: its been months to a year now since i got these. The earbuds battery life is okay. When i use them for a few hours and fall asleep with them on they will be at low battery in the morning. The Bluetooth range is still pretty good and better than my expensive headses. Having used plenty of headphones lately i felt it necessary to come back and mention the audio quality As i said before the sound isn't very loud and requires high volume. The audio quality is passable and i can't complain for the price i paid and i stick with saying do not pay more tban $50 for these. If its close to that price i would highly strongly suggest just dropping $10 more on some other earpods. The audio can get a bit of digital distortion if you pay close attention. I wore one philips in my right ear and put on my steelseries arctis gaming headset at the same time. Both had the same audio source playing and it was the first time i noticed that minor particle noise in the Philip's and further highlighted the low sound volume of the philips. But the steelseries is $200 the Philip's was $20

text: In general, I was happy with this set of earbuds. I purchased April 2016 and with irregular usage lasted till June 2018. To me, that's a good value on lifespan. However, I'd say avoid these. there are probably better deals at this point. I always keep my phone in my right front pocket and while using these, if I ever turned my head to the left, they'd lose signal and have to reconnect. The sound quality was alright, I'm not an audiophile though. Battery life was meh, I'd have to recharge the battery after every few days. I've retired this headset because the right ear piece is no longer working properly. I got caught in the rain while running one day and the headset seemed to be charging on without issue (this was on Wednesday) on Friday I tried to turn them on for my run and they wouldn't come on. I tried charging for a while and immediately heard crackling coming from the earbuds. I ran with a wired headset and when I got back, I checked the headset again, this time they were working just fine. On Monday the next week I tried to use them once again and they turned on without issue but there was still crackling coming from the right ear piece. it was also not producing much sound at all, the left was doing all the work. While it did rain, with an IPX4 rating, the ear buds should have been able to handle it no problem, they did not. Between the right ear piece failing (lost 1 star considering how long the headset lasted) and the not able to look left at all (this was a huge downer for me so it took 2 stars) I can only give this a 2 out of 5 and only that because they lasted me 2 years which is more than I expected for $80. TL;DR: if you enjoy having the ability to look left, don't buy these.

text: Everybody else is complaining about sound quality, so I won't waste my breath on that. I have another pair of noise-canceling headphones, full ear ones, that do a much better job and do not have the hiss problem. My main complaint about these earphones is the design of the main part with the switch and the battery housing. The location of the clip is really awkward. The clip points down, so I guess it is intended to go on your pants or belt. You have to tuck your shirt in to wear these earphones, like a dork. Otherwise, you put the battery compartment on your shirt, upside down, which shortens the already short cord. I am 5'9", so not freakishly tall by any measure, and the cord is so short it tugs and pulls, which is very irritating. The phones come with a little extension cord, but it does not solve the problem, since it extends the length of the cord below, not above the battery compartment. The other complaint I have is that the earphones make a noise every time you move. The fit between the cords and the ear buds is not good, so they create a crackling noise that is louder than whatever you are listening to. Every time the cords brush up against my shirt, I can hear it, amplified, through the earphones. Finally, I find that walking around in the wind is quite awful with these on. I often wear them with an iPod Shuffle when I go on walks outside, and whenever there is a gust of wind, it sounds like a jet engine is roaring in my ear. Again, the ear phones don't seem to be able to deal with those kinds of sudden, irregular noise bursts, even when it is white noise. I wouldn't buy them again, even though they were cheap the first time and have lasted me a good year so far.

text: The item was packaged and sent out on time (and the packaging was great). It didn't get to me on the scheduled delivery date, though - but that was not the fault of the shipper. This was a "Surepost" package - meaning UPS picks up the item and delivers it to your local post office, where the delivery itself is made by USPS. UPS ended up delivering this to the wrong post office, so there was a 2 day delay. Not the fault of the shipper at all, so I can't take off any points for something that wasn't their fault. The item itself was exactly as described - a bluetooth 4.0 USB "dongle". Works well with all items I've used it with - including a bluetooth headset, Blackberry phone, Motorola phone, PlayStation 4 controller, and connection to another PC in the house. Easy to install, use, and it works very well all-around. Range seems fine (although I've not measured any distances yet. Don't plan on it, either. It's Bluetooth....and works as a general Bluetooth module should). Used on a desktop PC with Windows 8.1 Pro x64 as the main operating system. Works well with generic Windows Bluetooth drivers, works even better with the drivers found on the disc this item comes with. UPDATE 12-3-15: One year later, still using this little unit and it works as well as it always has. In fact, it seems to work even better in Windows 10 than it did in Windows 7 or 8. Headphones, controllers, etc, always connect instantaneously when I need them connected. Good stuff!

text: I consider myself fairly experienced with a wide range of headphones and I try to kee expectations reasonable for a given price point. I don't find these to be a value at all. On the upside, they are very comfortable and Shure provides a wide range of inserts so you can swap as needed. I can wear for long periods of time with no discomfort. Cable attachment allowing swivel as a great idea. External noise isolation is more than adequate with being eerily quiet. I do like to have some awareness of my surrounding when music is low or off. I use a set of JH Audio JH-16 IEMs and they really cut out almost all external noise. Maybe too much for some situations. Now I understand that there are many very positive reviews based upon sound quality. That's one of the reasons I bought them. I don't get it at all. To me, they sounded overly warm to the point of somewhat muddy. Frequency definition was loose and bled together. Boring sound. Flat highs, forward miss and muddy bass. I've had lowest end Polk and midrange Senns that beat the heck out these in terms of clarity and accuracy, two or the areas most important to me. I will compliment the soundstage. It sounded very accurate to me. Live and studio music both have a realistic sense of scale and space. That part was nice. In short, there are so many other earbuds that really outshine these. I think the sound/comfort/cost ratio simply made these a poor value. I can get way better sounding buds for close to the same money or less. These really sounded to me like $16 Skull Candy buds. In contrast, I bought some Denon AH-C820s for $199 and they sound like $500+ competitors. They exceeded expectations while these really fell short. In fairness, I will say that I listened to these on both an iPhone 7 as well as an Onkyo DP-X1. These buds did sound moderately better on the Onkyo and likely would have gone from mediocre to pretty good if I swapped the cable for a balanced cable. Only problem is that I don't always carry the Onkyo and I would think it's not too much to get decent sound with an iPhone. I would think that the number of people using these buds with some kind of high-end player vs those with a traditional cell phone has got to be small. Way more people listening on a cell phone. That's why I am being so rough on these buds. I'm going to give them to my son and he will like them. He's a big bass fan when he listens to music and I think they do a respectable job there. I recommend you look elsewhere if you are committed to this price range. The Shures I would recommend are way out of this price range. If you were will to spend a little more for earbuds that far outperform way more expensive models, I highly recommend the afore-mentioned Denons. Purely my opinion... happy listening!

text: When I purchased these, I was almost sure that some of the specs were misleading for the price. Basically I wanted low latency headphones that had high sensitivity. I am pairing them with my Denon AVR S760H receiver to use at night. I had various other bluetooth headphones that had some latency issues at times, also the receiver did not have a variable bluetooth out and the signal was not very loud- hence this is why I needed something with high sensitivity. I can't guarantee that it is Bluetooth Version: V5.1, but I can tell you my latency issues are no longer- so it's possible that is correct. The sensitivity is rated at Sensitivity: 116.4±3dB and that seems fairly accurate, because I didn't need to turn these all the way up for decent audio levels. Then there is the actual sound. Since I'm using this on home theater, I am judging the sound on different movies/shows (not music)- undistorted strong clear bass, clear mids for dialog, and a nice smooth high end is what I was looking for - and this nailed it perfectly. It's pretty much all plastic (except the headband), the ear cushions feel nice, they rest outside the ear after maneuvering the headphones a bit for perfect fit. It doesn't have high clamping force and they are pretty comfortable. They look nice, but to pick them up you might get the impression that they feel cheap (because they are pretty light). Having said that, the lightness makes them a lot easier to tolerate for long periods of time- so really it's a positive not a negative. Really impressed for the money! Edit 1/28/22. Not sure why the bluetooth is now out of sync, and now has too much latency when watching TV (thru Denon AVR S760H ). I took off 2 stars for this because this was the primary reason I purchased these. I have a couple other bluetooth headphones with older bluetooth versions that work much better. Really bummed out, because initially they worked fine for a couple days. Unpaired and repaired them -nothing fixed it. Other than that they are really nice headphones Edit 2/2/22 Seller responded right away to my review. Offered to refund my purchase, or send me a new headphone. I like the headphones, so I opted from them to send me another set. These ones work perfect - I've used them several times over the past few days- no latency issues. Really appreciated how quickly the seller responded. They didn't suggest or tell me that I needed to change my review, they just wanted to make sure I was satisfied. Really impressed both with the product and the seller!

text: I'm coming from a 4 year old set of Jabra 65t-- which I love and are still working, but are starting to show it's age in battery life, so my review is based on comparisons between the two. This is very affordable option, but has a very basic feature set -- but the things it does, it does well (mostly). They are very comfortable and using the proper sized silicone ear tip allows for good noise blocking. The bluetooth connection is solid and has a bit more range than my 4 year old Jabras -- gives me about an extra 7 ft and can go through some more walls without issue. Audio quality is excellent for music and there is an optional app you can download to tweak EQ settings, limited customization of controls and will also show you battery level for each ear bud. It does not have active noise cancelling, but the silicone tips do a good job of blocking most outside noise. There are 4 tips included so you should be able to find one that fits your ear. It also does not have ambient mode (pass through mode) so take note that it will be tough to hear things around you, so may not be best for listening to music with these while out on a walk/run in the streets. I like that each ear can be used solo or together. The case is built well, and the earbuds are secured via magnets, so once you place them in, they are pretty secure and shouldn't fall out. The outside of the case is a little slippery in hand and has the capability of wireless charging. The one area that was severely lacking for me is the microphone quality. If you are in a quiet office room, then they will work fine. But if you are in an environment with any other background noise, these will not sound great. I am on the phone a lot for work, and that was the main selling point for me on the Jabra 65t's -- the microphone was stellar. Used them walking through airports, in the car, etc and they were the fantastic. TLDR: This is an affordable but basic pair of ear buds and great for audio listening. However, don't rely on these if you need to make voice calls with them, the microphone is terrible and you are better off putting the phone on speaker.

text: Like many others I had always wanted to see what all the hype was about with these ear buds, and with the cyber Monday crazy deal I couldn't resist. I'm comparing them to my S4s that I've use for the past 3+ years. Overall I was disappointed. I was hoping for a significant upgrade and these just are not. Don't get me wrong, for being so small they sound very good. They a tad crisper and clean sounding over the S4s. Bass is pretty good as well but not as good as the S4, just a tad smaller sounding. They play a bit louder then the S4s at the same volume but as others have mentioned, they tend to distort the louder you play them. The S4s sound better at high volumes and I don't think I've every heard them distort. Also they need a good break-in period and after a week the sound has improved, sounding even cleaner. They are very small and light and feel even better then the S4s in your ears. If you work out or run I'd say they would work better then the S4s. If you like to sleep with ear buds then most would be pretty happy with these. I sleep with them just about every day. So should you upgrade from your precious S4s? Depends. If you're looking for a nice upgrade in sound then you will most likely be disappointed. Again they sound very good, just not as FULL sounding as the S4s. If you need some really small ear buds for working out, running, every day commuting then I think you'd be happy with them... BUT not at there retail price. I'd say go for it if you can pick them up for less the a benjamin. One last note. The cord on these are very thin, even more so then the S4s. They tend to have more cord noise too and can get pretty tangled. Not a deal breaker for me as I'm really good with my stuff. End the end I have replaced my S4s with these and use them as my daily drivers. If you get them just play them none stop for at least two day so they can break-in. Then tend to sound better and better over time. Cheers!

text: The biggest issue I have with these is that I have rather small ears. The actual opening, not the canal. I bought them for running, but even with the smallest ear-wings, they felt like they were stuffed into my ears. After about 30mins, my ears would hurt and ring (more) due to the pain. And you can't just remove the ear-wings as there's sharp plastic that's used to hold the silicone one. Just a bad design for anyone with smallish ears. The other issue was, the left earbud would sometimes lower in volume--and this is with proper sealing tips (I love IEMs so I make sure I get a good seal). That's a defect in the left earbud. Otherwise, these are great if you know what you're getting. They've got GOBS of battery in the charging case so you can just forget to charge them for a long time, but the case is big. I'd say these are great in a bag or around the hose because of that. The sound is great--sounds exactly like Anker Soundcore's Liberty line. However, there's no EQ features--that's a bummer. To address the folks that have not used headphones with wires of varying lengths, this product is made to go behind your head, keeping the wires out of the way. I tried to call friends, colleagues and myself (answering machine at home, other cell phone's voice mail, work voice mail), but my voice was always "far away" and mixed with noise: and this in the best situation possible, that is, myself alone in a perfectly quiet room. As soon as I drove my car (which is *very* quiet), entered a normal room or just walked outside, people at the other side of the communication could not hear me. The only way to speak to them was to remove the headset from my ear and put the microphone in front of my mouth (but I could not hear them anymore). I use a lot my cell phone and I need to be able to talk to people and have a clear communication, so this headset was a no-go for me. Maybe my unit was defective, even though I read other reviews with similar problems with the microphone. Anyway, if it comes for free with the phone, you can always give it a shot, but before paying for it, make sure that my case was (or is) and isolated one. On the positive side, I never had a problem with returns to Amazon.com, which in my opinion is a very reliable place to buy from, so if you buy it here you can be sure you can return it within 30 days with no problems (they pay for shipping it back if the item is defective). text: Wow. Fantastic sound!! Great clarity and definition. Tons of low-end but the mids and highs are still there and sound smooth and pleasant. Fit is comfortable and decent. I do like how Sure and Westone fit a bit better but the Future Sonics are lighter in weight so they seem to disappear better than the other brands. Plenty of ear tip options included to help getting a proper seal in your ear and there is also a nice semi-hard zippered case. My only gripe is that there seems to be a bump in the 80 to 120hz range that causes the low-end to be a bit bloated. This can be tamed for home listening, but on the stage for IEM use (my true intended purpose) I found that upper-low frequency bump to be overwhelming, blurring the separation and tonality of the instruments/vocals in the mix, making it difficult to perform with both buds in my ears. Not ideal. If Future Sonics could tame that one issue of upper low-end bloat, then I would say the G10's would be an absolute no-brainer as in all other respects, as they sound better than any single driver earbuds have a right to, and certainly better than a host of more expensive 2 and 3 driver ear buds I have used. I'd say worth a listen for sure as they could easily win you over.

text: It's difficult to quantify all the merits of a really good pair of headphones because at the end of the day, the sound they generate is subject to user preference. There are, however, expectations and baseline specs that should be met to be classified as a pair of audiophile/professional headphones even before beginning to critique the finer characteristics that make each headphone unique. Performance: Astell&Kern re-engineered Beyerdyamic's very accurate, 2nd generation T1 Tesla tranducers to perform at a lower impedance of 32ohm without losing its 5hz-50khz frequency range. The lower impedance allows the listener to drive the headphones with pretty much any portable player or amp. The sound characteristics stay consistent through different levels of amplitude and distortion is not an issue even beyond uncomfortable listening levels. Its nominal sound pressure level is 102db for anyone curious. The performance is bookended by its precice audio imaging and exact stereo separation. Construction & Materials: This set is hand-built in Germany. It features the Tesla T1 drivers which are seated at an angle inside the baffle behind a metal construction. The housing is a combination of hard plastic and metal that is capped by a delicate, woven, metallic grill with the Astell&Kern badge. The sliding arm and hangers are also made of metal that extend to the very supple, top-grain leather headband. The arm has two points of articulation that allow for pivot and swivel. High grade metal parts of the housing have a soft touch tinanium finish contrasted with a brushed titanium finish on the arm. Earpads are made of slow recovery foam covered by velour. The entire package is topped off by two professional grade, detachable audio cables; a 3-pole cable that terminates to 3.5mm connector and a balanced 4-pole cable that terminates to a 2.5mm connector. Ergonomics: The AK T1p headphone is light. Even with the large drivers and the metal construction, Beyerdynamic and Astell&Kern are able to create a portable pair of headphones for long listening sessions without neck fatigue. The earpad has been engineered to draw heat away from the listener for extended comfort. Out of the box caliper pressure is decent. It's neither too tight nor too loose. The cables are made of light materials which don't add too much to the total weight of the headphones. The distance between the listener's ear and the audio drivers is also quite nice and reduces listening fatigue. Sound Quality: This is where things start to lean towards subjectivity, but let's talk about my listening experience. The headphones provide an pretty nice sense of space and staging. The sound stage isn't so wide that it alters the intent of the recording; it feels just right. Sound imaging and location properties are quite precise and very distinguishable. It is able to render three dimensionality and clear stereo separation. The sound signature has a nice balance through its frequency range. It has great extension at the highs and provides air and sparkle at the appropriate frequencies. Unwatend sibilance is non-existent. The highs are crisp and pleasant. Mid frequencies provide some warmth, but not enough to classify these as warm sounding headphones. It's just enough to lay down a nice foundation for the high frequencies and maintain a natural sounding balance with the lower frequencies. The very controlled mids result in clarity in the vocal range and little to no bleed into the bass. Bass response is fast, controlled, and very tight. It's able to extend to sub frequencies without over emphasizing the sound. The sound signature is well balanced, but definitely not neutral. As accurate as these headphones are, they are more appropriate and made for critical music listening. I wouldn't recommend these for professsional mixing. All things considered (including the price) these headphones mark every checkbox of what an audiophile class pair headphones should deliver and have the bonus of being made with portability in mind. This is one of the best out there.
product_title: Astell&Kern AK T1p Balanced Semi-Open Back Stereo Headphones with Tesla Drivers by Beyerdynamic

text: I as a monthly traveller and bought these primarily for plane trips and also for the occasional bus commute. After 17 months I'm looking for a replacement. Summary: they may seem like a good deal relative to Bose, but they are not very durable (even with careful, non-daily use) despite the seemingly-solid build. What's good: nice packaging, they "feel" very solid. Cords don't tangle in the clamshell carrying case, and in addition to the variety of included ear adaptors you can also buy third-party ones to get a perfect fit. Also, they use replaceable AAA batteries so you can always keep a couple of spares in the carrying case. This does make the "dongle" larger and heavier than those with a built-in battery (which did not bother me). What's OK: the noise cancellation, most of the time. There certainly is better out there (Bose) but for the price I was happy with what they provided. What's not good: Durability. The microphone stopped working after a few months, and now I'm getting "crackles" whenever anything moves. This is despite what I'd describe as *very* moderate use- there are months when I don't use them at all, at most I was using them weekly. I am careful with my electronics, and I folded them cautiously and stored in the included carrying case whenever they weren't in use. Noise cancellation fails in two cases: in windy conditions they produce "microphone in the wind" noise, and when a plane reverses thrust upon landing the system starts clipping due to the loud noise and you get loud popping noises. Sound quality is very mediocre; perfectly fine for inattentive listening and movies and such, but if you have an ear for good speakers or headphones you'll find yourself wanting to use other phones if you don't need the actual noise cancellation.

text: I have bought 3 pairs of Samsung earbuds. The first pair were the Galaxy Buds Pro. First off the design of these is awful. They are very heavy and did not stay in my ears. About the only way to keep them in is if you were to wear a bandana on your head around your ears. I jog every day and these fell out just sitting down. None of the different size rubber fittings worked in my ear with them either. The Bluetooth connection is also awful. As soon as I put my phone in my pocket it cut out. I literally has to hold my phone by my shoulder to get it to work without any problems. I have a Samsung phone so I wanted to have earbuds from the same company as I really like my phone. I even tried connecting them to other Bluetooth devices in my home such as my T.V. and sound bar and still they didn't work unless I was standing right on top of the device I was connected to. I ended up returning them as they were useless to me. I was very disappointed in Samsung as a company. After some time and thought I decided to try the Samsung Galaxy Buds Live. Once I received them and put them in my ears I was happy to find that they fit my ears much better than the Galaxy Buds Pro ones did. Unfortunately, after connecting them to my phone I found the same problem with the Bluetooth as before. As soon as I tried to put my phone in my pocket the Bluetooth cut right out. I even tried them with other Bluetooth devices like I did with the others. It was still cutting out. I was again very frustrated and disappointed at the same time. Hoping that maybe it was a factory defect I returned them for a replacement pair. Upon receiving the replacement pair it had exactly the same problem as the previous pair. So now I have returned them for a full refund. This was my third pair and third try at getting a pair of Samsung earbuds. When I called Samsung customer service and tried to explain what was going on it was very hard to understand the individual who was trying to assist me. I asked to speak to someone else so I could understand what was being said. All I was offered was to return the last pair that I had purchased so then could repair them for me or I could be refunded my money. I don't think they understood that after three pair that were all having the same issue I wasn't seeing a point to returning a brand new pair to them for them to "fix". So all I had left for an option was a refund than I am currently on my second week of waiting to receive my money back. I am a Samsung person and really wanted to have matching ear buds from the same company. Unfortunately, this seems to be impossible as I am not willing to take a fourth chance with Samsung hoping that they finally get it right. I don't believe that Samsung has gone out of their way or above and beyond to resolve this situation they clearly have with their products. I have had gotten better use and better quality using my wired Apple Ear buds than anything from Samsung. If the company can not see a way to fix my situation it looks like I may be becoming an Apple product person instead. I just want other people who are considering buying either of these Samsung products to be aware of their poor quality and problems and the company's awful efforts to make good on their products.

text: Sorry folks, I posted my review below for a different listing by the same seller. Both listings had the same exact single image and opposite product titles when I purchased them (one headset from each listing at slightly different pricing and with different product titles. Link to this listing follows: [[ASIN:B002TZAAT0 OEM RIM Blackberry Stereo Hands-free Headset with On/off Button for BlackBerry Curve 8300/ 8310/ 8320 - HDW-14322-001]] While these may appear to be similar to an authentic Blackberry earbud headset, they are not. These have a substantially larger and thicker build all around and appear to be made well enough - although time will tell. These completely lack the much more polished "refined" design of my authentic Blackberry headsets. The earbuds on these advertised Blackberry Factory Original or OEM headsets are substantially larger. Their earbuds are identical - meaning that both R and L are the same without any distinction in shape, while the authentic version earbuds are more fitted to each respective ear. The backs of these OEM earbuds feature silver pyramid-like adornments, of which are not present on either of my Blackberry headsets. The OEM cord melds together much higher around the neck - leaving far less slack for movement in stark contrast to the real deal. The photo looks like an authentic Blackberry earbud headset, but, clearly - they are not the same. I can hear through them which is a good start, although, I have yet to test its mic. The earbuds are uncomfortable due to their larger size, but, I bought these for the hands-free speaking-option rather than listen to music or media. Under three bucks with fast free USPS shipping/tracking - packed safely in a bubble envelope - definitely something to consider; although, I am not happy that these are a knock-off product being advertised as an authentic Blackberry headset (totally misleading as false advertising). Before receiving one set, I ordered another from this same seller (different listing with different price, but, same single image as mentioned above) as a back-up pair. My back-up headset is the same exact knock-off product as the "OEM" model. I contacted this seller (Seller1ON1) about advertising this headset as a genuine Blackberry headset (which is totally misleading as false advertising) and shipping out a counterfeit product. Their customer service is prompt, pleasant and efficient. They sent me a replacement headset, and, unfortunately -- it is also the same identical counterfeit Blackberry headset. Based upon my principle of getting what I paid for (in this case, an authentic Blackberry product), I filed an A-to-z claim and was refunded my purchase amount in the form of a gift card. I thought these would be real after reading reviews, but, alas - I returned to re-read those that stated such. These much older reviews must reflect a time when these were indeed authentically Blackberry. If you check out this seller's (Seller1ON1) storefront and search for Blackberry, you will discover the multiple listings this seller has for the same pair of knock-off Blackberry headsets with different product titles, images and pricing. I nicked four stars for being a counterfeit Blackberry headset.

text: UPDATE 12/9/17: So I've had a lot more time to evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of this headphone and can honestly say its best suited to traditional warm sounding tube amps such as the WA2 or even the newer WA8 or Bottlehead Crack. Vocals come across as a bit too sharp which can get fatiguing on modern music which already has boosted treble. What I have noticed, though, since correcting the V-dip in the upper 10-14k region is the soundstage is much wider - much more closer to the 800s. I finally understand what the appeal for the 800s is - it's great for layered instrumental music like Classical or Bebop Jazz. These headphones with the Seatbelts or instrumental beats really give you insight as to how the composer made the track. It's incredible detailed - reverbs come across with their natural decay - cymbals have the right sharpness and shimmer to them, harmonica's come across as incredibly vibrant with the air between the artists breaths taking shape. Get these headphones for Jazz, Gaming, and Acoustic. Guitars sound wonderful with ultimate clarity and weighty bass like they do in real life. Not really recommended for heavy vocal tracks like Rap, Pop, Country, etc. unless paired with a warm amp like the Liquid Carbon or Woo Audio WA2. Everyone likes to take shots at the 700's and I almost bought into the hype. I'm glad I didn't. When I first hooked this up into my Modi 2 Multibit and Magni 3 it sounded muffled and not at all what people told me. Then I realized adding a warm DAC to a warm amp is going to sound terrible. After switching out the amp to a Solid State (Aune T1), these have easily beaten my other headphones by a mile (HD600's, 598s, 400is). The 700s are mini HD800s without their vast soundstage. They are sharp, clear, and have a great amount of detail retrieval. To be able to make the most of these cans you really have to make sure your source material is Hi Rez enough at 320 or FLAC if possible. On FLAC recordings, you'll begin to hear the saliva of the artist, the various instruments cues and imaging going on around you, and a remarkable competence in very busy tracks with no effort on the 700's part in delivering the sound to your ears. On well recorded YouTube videos, you'll hear the person gulp as they clear their throats or a ruffling of papers. The detail is excellent for the price you pay. What I love most about these cans is even with all this detail and sharpness - they're not fatiguing or sibilant no matter what the naysayers say. If you pair this to the right system (not an O2+ODAC, essentially you'll want an OTL amp or warmer amp like the Liquid Carbon) you'll hear a musical sound with the treble energy and sharpness you expect in this lineup. This thing literally leans more towards the HD800 side than the 650 side but in a good way (without all the downsides of the 800s). All that being said, this gave me a real itch to upgrade to the 800's. Once you taste some of the best you want to know what the best has to offer. I've experimented with several equalizers that turn the 700's into similar sounding 800s and honestly it gives you a glimpse of what the 800s do better which is that they are even brighter, sharper, and the little muted sounds of the air between the artist reading lyrics, twitches of a violin swinging between one note to another, flipping pages as you sit in a concert hall, etc. become all the more noticeable. Having collected lots of Classical Music when I was younger, I'm almost certain I will be getting the 800s as well to compare. All I can say is these have dethroned my modded 400is as my new daily drivers. Comfort, size, looks, standard connector (2.5mm mono, easy to replace because it's non-propeitary [in fact I swapped it for my 400is cable] and sharp clarity while still letting me relax but be able to hear the lyrics in their entirety is an experience it its own right. Huge fan of what Sennheiser did here. Don't let the naysayers who say this thing is too bright sway you. They don't know what they're talking about and most likely didn't research properly prior to buying these. While these may not be as picky as an 800 in getting an amp and source material right they really do benefit from the right equipment and as they say garbage in = garbage out. So, take it from me - if you amp this thing properly, you'll love 'em. -Will come back to this review after pairing this with the Valhalla 2 to come up with my final impressions EDIT: So I've had a few days with the Valhalla 2 and Mimby combo with these cans and they really smooth out the sound. The Valhalla drives these cans with authority and it's a great pairing. It honestly sucked a little too much out of the sound for my liking so I equalized a bit. Below are my EqualizerAPO settings after a LOT of experimentation. I believe these are the ideal settings as they eliminate the V dip in the upper frequency response 8-15k range and increase the soundstage and sharpness by a lot, thus preserving the original character of these cans - they bring a ton of fun energy which sounds great with metal, trap, or cymbal music or music with mids that need sharp, clarity and accentuation without going overboard. Through my testing, these headphones respond really well to equalization. You can turn them into deep bass machines or really laid back cans. I'd expect nothing less from one of Sennheisers best dynamic drivers! text: First things first, these have awesome packaging in that they're easy to open. I feel the need to mention this because some things are so crazy, that easy open stuff makes me happy. Okay onto the real issue at hand, the headset. To me it just looks like an old school set of headphones but with a slimmed down band which feels almost flimsy because it has quite a bit of give to it. The wireless aspect means that there is a detachable dongle connected to the left earcup. These are really light with or without the dongle attached. If you remove the dongle you can use them wired, but you lose the ability to make calls and there are the usual playback controls on the dongle, well you obviously lose those too. I had two main sets of heaphones I was using when they arrived -- both with mic capabilities but I only cared that one had a mic as it was paired with my phone, the other was paired with a computer being used as headphones for music and videos. One, [[ASIN:B0070UKBO8 MEElectronics Air Fi Runaway Bluetooth Stereo Wireless Headphones with Microphone (Black/Red)]], I was happy with. The other, not so much. I figured this could replace the pair I was unhappy with. The only question for me was would it end up on the computer where the mic doesn't matter or with the phone where it does? The truth is the jury is still out on that. So far the MeElectronics seems to be winning mic wise as the person I actually talk to the most and the longest noticed a difference. She wondered what had changed. When I explained I was calling to test a new set of headphones, I had to explain I wanted to see if they were better/worse/no different from the ones I usually used. The first call was a disaster but she was in a loud place so we chalked that up to issues on her end. When she called back it was better but she still felt it was different - she could hear me but she felt like it was as though I had her on speakerphone. With the AirFi she said she had no clue that I was anything other than the phone's direct mic. Since she could actually hear me it's not an issue, I chalk it up to the mic being better placed on the other brand. When it comes to audio, I've had no complaints whether I was listening to various types or music or audiobooks though I am not some crazed audiophile who can tell you how much more of this setting or that something needs to be "right" or "perfect" or whatever. These are as comfortable as the MeElectronics (my faves comfort wise). They're light, should fit just about any adult. Decent sized earcups. Although I was a little taken aback by the whole dongle thing at first, being set up there is nice in that unlike some other headphones I have, they don't necessarily become useless when they need to charge. You can disconnect the dongle and charge it while using them wired. The controls are easy to use / figure out, the manual is possibly not even needed as they're pretty standard (up and down volume buttons and then one button for everything else). Of the headphone/headsets I own, they're tied with MEElectronics AirFi as my new faves. They're both really comfortable (a huge deal to me as I have frequent headaches and ear infections, etc). This has a slight advantage soundwise and it keeps sound both in and out better. AirFi has a slight advantage when it comes to the mic. If the two were to somehow merge, they'd be perfect. As it is, this pair is really decent.

text: I have always enjoyed listening to far away AM stations at night (DXing) and this radio is one of the better ones for that purpose, even compared to much more expensive radios. It is simple to use with a large internal ferrite antenna. I have never connected it to an external antenna (screws for this are on the back) or antenna tuner, which I imagine would improve reception. Most new radios have digital synthesized tuners and while that adds tuning accuracy, it often adds noise that is bad for DXing. This radio is not the best built and has known quality control issues such as tuning inaccuracies that can be rectified. It isn't tiring to listen to because it has good sound quality due to the large main speaker, tweeter and bass/treble controls. The FM section works very well too. I do not DX FM so can't comment on it's long distance capabilities but it sounds good and holds the stations well. It uses long running D cells but I use the internal AC power supply - the AC cord is permanently attached. There are many reviews of this storied radio on the net you can read so I won't go on and on. It looks like the RCA model replaced the GE but I imagine it is the same radio other than the name on the front. I was fortunate to find a Superadio II at a thrift store and enjoy that earlier model as well.

text: My first impression of these were not very good, they sent me the wrong color. That aside, my first impression of the build quality was very good. High grade resin from Germany, they felt stronger and more solid than metal housings, which can be cold and uncomfortable at first touch. Packaging was decent with 3 different ear tip styles, and a pair of double flanged eartips in size m. Sound: General sound impressions were that these were warm, laid back, and jazzy. Sweet and smooth sound. Excellent detail without being too bright with a W shaped sound, and some mid-bass bloat/bleeding. Highs were never sibilant, but could have used a bit more extension or sparkle. Detail was very good. Upper mids were also very good, lots of detail, and intimate with forward vocals. Lower mids was a bit disappointing, the mid bass bled into the lower mids, causing the songs to sound muddled and congested in this area. Mid-bass was bloated, but I just turned my eq down about 3-4 decibels. Bass had good extension, with insanely good layers and really good speed of attack. However, due to the nature of the Fa7's using only balanced armatures, it lacked the thump that a dynamic driver would have given. I loved listening to edm (certain songs), jazz, pop, and rock with these. Two Feet's "Had Some Drinks" sounded absolutely insane on these the Scripts "Man on a wire" also sounded great on these, as the bass has a strong presence with light impact. Other edm with more dynamic range sounded poor on these. Hip hop, and more modern music like "Black Beatles" sounded meh. The sound is so sweet, and smooth, I would find excuses to just listen to music on these. If you're looking for modern music, my recommendations are the fh5 or the ikko oh1. (the ikko oh10s are out, but I dont know enough about those yet.)

text: I’m no audiophile but found the sound quality from the Sennheiser CX Sport Headphones to be excellent for an in-ear headphone. The Bluetooth was easy to pair and is quick to connect. The battery life is good. I get 5 or 6 hours of play between charges. The headphones block out a good amount of noise. I’ve been wearing the CX Sport headphones while doing yard work and I can still hear my music while using a gas powered lawn mower. My major issue with the Sennheiser CX Sport headphones is they don’t stay in my ears. I’ve tried all of the different ear pieces and I can’t get any of them to stay in my ear unless I keep my head still. I would expect an in-ear sport headphone to stay in my ears better. This is a common problem for me with sport headphones. I’ve only been able to keep headphones that loop over my ear from moving around when I run or work in the year. Overall, if you don’t normally have issues with in-ear headphones staying in your ear you will be happy with the Sennheiser CX Sport headphones quality.

text: Just replaced a pair of Boise QC-20s that got crushed. Decided to try out the Beoplay E4 based on reviews and that they were $50 less. Based on the reputation of Bang & Olufsen, I thought these stood a good chance to be a decent replacement for the QC-20s. The should quality is good the issue is the noise cancellation is pretty much non-existent. On the 1-10 noise cancellation scale the QC-20s are a 7 and the Beoplay E4s are a 2. I had multiple people try them out to make sure it wasn't just me, all were in agreement or thought they were worse than I did. When you turn the noise cancellation on the outside noises were marginally softer, notice I don't say quieter. They are more comfortable to wear than the QC-20s but that's not a reason for paying $200. Bottom line - not acceptable at the cost.

text: I purchased the Rimor and was then offered a test for the B530. Enjoyed doing a comparison of the two! The fit of course was the same, both provided a choice of a tight, snug fit which pretty much buffered all outside noise, even the motor on my F250 truck. So yes to both for noise cancellation quality. Wind and background noise still carries over to phone conversations, my roosters rule if I'm outside on a phone call. The smaller tips I found more comfortable, but that is definitely personal preference. The smaller producing a looser fit and if heavily jarred can drop out. I'm not a runner so can't confirm the tightness there but I have had very few times that they have dropped and usually because I have not inserted well. As far as music, for ear buds both the Rimor and the B530 are exceptional. If you like bass like I do then the B530 is the way. I have not had the batteries run done as yet - At this point I have to take Tranya's promises on battery life. With both the storage in the ear bud and in the case and don't see them falling short on that promise. Takes a bit of practice to take the earbuds out of the case as the cutout to slide your finger into is for a pretty small finger. Packaging is quality for sure and the case will hold up and protect the earbuds from damage without a problem. All in all the music quality for these earbuds is fantastic but is not superior to the use of full ear headphones. That is something I don't think one can ever expect. Voice quality for phone usage (which is my primary use) has been great, I have no complaints. I prefer the Rimor's "not so deep" fit. Calls are easy to answer and to disconnect. The slight touch on the bud itself works well. Changing the volume while on a call or listening to music is a bit challenging but that seems to be a "user" problem and error and not a fault of the ear bud! Yes, I would absolutely recommend these ear buds. Both Rimor and B530 are excellent. Rimor: 1) Case is somewhat smaller and can easily go in your jeans pocket. B530: 1) Deeper bass tones. A slightly deeper fit than the Rimor so does hold in the ear a bit tighter.
product_title: [Upgraded Version] TRANYA B530 Bluetooth 5.0 Deep Bass True Wireless Earbuds, Aptx/AAC Compatible Sports Wireless Headphone with CVC8.0 Noise Cancellation, 80 Hours Playtime with Charging Case

The only problem with this is that the 250 will easily fall out of the holder and if you use it you WILL lose it. It is only a matter of time. My 250 lasted about 45 seconds and when I went to get it from the belt clip it was GONE. Not the holder but the 250 itself. Some lucky stiff at the Houston airport picked it up and walked away. text: Wow!! Just received today. Don't know where to start. These are truly fantastic in every regard! I listen to all kinds of music and have owned expensive stereo systems in my car and home. This review concerns using the HA-RX500's listening to music through my PC. I am very particular about quality. I want to hear all the details in a piece of recorded music and want background parts at the right sound level in relation to the other instruments/vocals in a song. These headphones have AMAZING sound--not for $20--just amazing sound in their own right. I read a review that said they have better sound quality than a $120 pair of headphones, and I couldn't agree more. Sound is rich and full. Can hear all layers of all types of music. Bass is very impressive as are the highs, but what truly impressed me, and which I have found lacking in two other sets of headphones I recently ordered, is the quality of the mid-range sounds. The headphones are incredibly light-feeling on your head and the ear pads are soft and very, very comfortable. The long cord is absolutely no problem and looks and feels substantive, unlike some other cheap, very thin cords. They are excellent at outside sound dampening. I researched so many headphones for hours and bought a pair of JVC HAV-570 "Super Bass" headphones. Admittedly, they were only $13, but they had many of the same specs as the X500's, i.e., 40mm drivers, etc, but the sound on the X500'S is literally five times better, and this saying a lot, because I was mildly satisfied with the cheaper pair (which got four stars overall on Amazon). However, wanting more, I purchased a pair of Audio-Technica ATH-M30 Professional Headphones through Amazon for $40. They lacked range and were tight and felt smothering when worn. They don't come close to the JVC X500 in sound quality. I returned them and was going to settle for the other JVC's until I saw these on Amazon). I am not an expert at describing what makes for high sound quality but I know that when someone says, when describing headphones, that they hear parts of songs they couldn't previously hear well with other headphones, that means something, if accurate. That description is absolutely true with these headphones. It's not so much you will hear sounds that you never heard at all, it is that you will hear instrumental parts and vocals (such as some back up vocals), much clearer and stronger than you hear them with other headphones. I must re-emphasize that the sound from these headphones is incredibly rich and full, especially if your system has a graphic equalizer that you can admust to your particular likes. You cannot go wrong with these headphones!! I am almost in disbelief that they cost only $18, seem solidly made, are extremely comfortable and the sound will impress you to no end. They are heaven!

text: I purchased these recently because a friend also had this model. I had an opportunity to check them out and thought the audio quality was incredible. But this review is an argument against giving into an impulse buy. I use earbuds almost constantly around the shop as well as for recreational use at home. They're primarily for listening to music and talking on my cellphone. They pair up with my Samsung Galaxy S4 with no difficulty and I find that I can leave the phone in a central location and move around the workspace with no drops or fades. They are comfortable and seem to fit snuggly. The audio quality is good with impressive low end response and no distortion. Good for day to day use. My main gripe with the Powerbeats2 is the lack of APT-X support. I want to be able to watch TV using them and the way they work right now makes it all but impossible. There is at least a 500ms lag between the image on the TV and the buds. Unacceptable performance for such supposedly high end headphones.Re-pairing has no effect the problem persists. So if you are considering them for this application I recommend you look elsewhere. There are many alternatives, mostly far cheaper than this model. Yes, I know I should have checked for APT-X before I ordered. Forgive me for assuming that such a comparatively expensive product support the 4.0 codec and APT-X. I wonder if a firmware update from Beats could add this? I have read a number of reviews that say they are fragile and prone to cracking. As well as failure of the switches that control volume and pause. I haven't had that problem so far but reserve the right to amend my review if I find this to be the case. As it stands they get a solid 3 stars but are not worth the money. Addendum: After using these for a month they started to drop blutooth signal from my Galaxy S4. Especially when I am using them out doors. Don't know what that is about. It's too late to replace them through Amazon so now I have to deal with Apple customer service. Not sure what to expect.

text: I was super excited about these headphones, because they're the first pair of super deluxe headphones that I've ever owned. But, unfortunately, they perform worse than my headphones that I got at 1/4th of the price. They're also nowhere near the quality of similarly priced headphones that I've tried. So my 2 stars are based mostly on that a unit like this should really cancel out the noise. Maybe I got a bad unit, though, because I think a lot of other people have liked these headphones. Pros: +I have a ringing in my ear, and so noise cancelling headphones that cancel out all of the noise makes my ear ringing sound really loud. These headphones provide a bunch of white noise, as part of the noise cancellation, so I can't hear my ear ringing. +There's a button to resample the ambient noise, and it's supposed to give you a better noise cancelling. I'm not sure if it works or not, but it's cool they put a button that makes you feel like you have some control. +There's a little Braille-like knob over the left ear. I didn't think I'd use it, but it's actually cool, to be able to tell if you have the headphones on right. +Looks expensive +Fits nice on my head Cons: -When I put these down, the power button and power light are on the bottom of the unit, so I don't have a visual cue that I left the power on. I've burned through a bunch of batteries with these because I accidentally left the power on overnight. -The "Monitor" button is a joke. text: I just purchased these headphones as a replacement for the junky basic set that came with my Ipod Nano (3G). If all you take from this review is that these are *way* better than what you received with your Ipod, you can stop reading now. If you want more detail, please continue... On with the details --- I read several reviews of many more and less expensive sets of in-ear (canal) headphones. In every case I found that there was both good and bad. I saw hundreds of reviews for headphones that cost triple (or more) what these cost. I was tempted to buy a more expensive set, but am now very glad I didn't. If you're like me, you just want a decent set of headphones that sound pretty good, fit comfortably, and be sturdy enough to be used on a daily basis. Likewise, they need to be inexpensive enough to not make you cringe if you accidentally break or lose them. Again, I'd recommend this set of headphones if you fit those requirements. Tonight I bought two sets of headphones and tried them both. There was this set, which was at Walmart for about $16, and then a set of Koss KE29S canal earphones. The Koss set cost about $26 at Walmart. The Koss set had a frequency response of 15-20,000 Hz. This set is marked as being 8Hz - 23,000Hz. The Koss set had an built in volume slider, which is always nice. Both sets had the "squishy" ear inserts. The sensitivity and impedance were the same on both. You'll find all sorts of opinions online about whether or not these numbers matter. The frequency response, in my opinion, makes a difference. I tried the Koss set first, and they definitely sounded good. After about 10-15 minutes with those, I plugged in the JVC marshmellow set. It wasn't like night and day, but the JVC set sounded brighter, and more "in your face" than the Koss set. Both fit my ears comfortably and tightly, so I doubt the fit would have made any difference. At this point, I'd decided that the sound was enough of a reason to ditch the Koss set and do more testing with the JVC set. On the JVC - I heard no distortion at 80% of the Ipod Nano's maximum volume while playing everything from Young Jeezy, Jack Johnson, and the Dropkick Murphys, to groups such as OAR and K's Choice. I also tried a few "talk radio" style podcasts. As for how they fit and feel, I'd say they're very comfortable. I used the standard ear piece that came on them, although it comes with a larger set. The seal is tight, and I can "feel" the bass comfortably enough. I used them while driving and didn't hear anything else. These definitely keep outside noise at bay well enough for most users. Oh, you don't look like "Shrek" when you wear these either (look at Shrek's pictures and you'll see what I mean). The JVCs seemed to have a lower profile than some of the others that were available. The length of the cord seems appropriate. Both sides are equal length, and the Ipod Nano fit comfortably in my pants pocket with a few inches in length to spare. There's not a ton of excess cord that you have to fumble with. Between the comfort in my ears and the length of the cord, I think these would be ideal for exercising (running, rowing or lifting in my case). Are these the best sounding headphones out there? I'm sure they aren't. The guy that spent $100 on headphones will never admit he spent too much on a similar sounding set and will always be hyper critical and a perfectionist about what they (or others) buy. For my money, these JVC's meet all my criteria and offer both the sound and cost that I can live with and be happy. Thanks!
